tasks.short: Direct wardrobe crews during rehearsals or performances

steps.what: Read the actual current dressing list, cast changes and scene cues through existing scene and performer filters
inputs: Actual current dressing list and rehearsal or performance changes
outputs: Verified current wardrobe context

steps.what: Direct the actual wardrobe crew through spoken cues during the rehearsal or performance, respond to costume changes and resolve immediate dressing problems
inputs: Actual live performance, crew and costume-change conditions
outputs: Actual crew direction and resolved or escalated wardrobe issues

steps.what: Write the actual existing rehearsal or performance cue note after events, using the native scene and performer fields and retaining actual problem descriptions
inputs: Actual observed wardrobe events and verified scene and performer identifiers
outputs: Actual cue and wardrobe-issue entry

steps.what: Save the actual cue note in the same wardrobe record
inputs: Completed actual cue entry
outputs: Stored cue note

tasks.design: Configure {OPS_SYSTEM}, the existing wardrobe list and cue record, to filter actual scenes and performers and reuse their identifiers in the actual cue note. Live crew direction stays with the attendant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the current scene context and repeating scene identifiers can interrupt rehearsal work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scene views and entry fields can reduce that clerical effort.
tasks.still_hard: Immediate costume problems depend on the actual performance and crew.
tasks.human_edge: Communicate a workable adjustment quickly without losing track of performers.

ambition.what: Support the existing live wardrobe-direction episode.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: wardrobe scene lists can be filtered and their identifiers reused in existing cue records; live crew direction remains human work.

assumptions: Representative rehearsal/performance episode with an actual existing cue note. No new report after every conversation is invented. The actual wardrobe planning staff produce scene and cast lists in normal work; s1 counts reading and checking current changes, s2 live direction and s3 actual subsequent record writing.

S3 savings cover existing scene/performer fields only, not interpreting live issues. No free correct dressing list is assumed; mismatches remain human checks. Try native views and templates first; features already used have no new benefit.

S2 is actual spoken crew direction. S3 records events, not a concealed new operative assignment or emailed instruction. A real written assignment release or message needs its own final version and actual authority before a separate send; it is not hidden in the save.

Ordinary same-system save share1 is negligible, fully retained and ungated, with no saving or author self-approval. Shares are illustrative task work independent of prompt time priors; list preparation is counted at its real frequency rather than charged anew to every cue.
unknowns: Are scene filters and cue-entry identifiers already linked?
What actual cue writing is required during this production?
research_questions: Observe actual wardrobe direction and separate scene lookup, spoken cues and existing cue-record writing.

already_counted.description: Actual scene checking, live crew direction, retained cue-entry production and ordinary save remain in s1-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain scene-to-entry links beyond retained rehearsal-specific checking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:15*.20+14*.10=4.4 gross less1 upkeep=3.4. Low: the live dressing list already has direct scene navigation, so its15 points yield no new gain; actual cue fields still save1.4, less1 upkeep=.4. All70 live-direction and1 save points remain, and cue meaning stays human. Unmeasured existing-scene-view case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Collect actual alteration jobs, deadlines, worker availability and relevant skills and verify the scheduling period and explicit availability constraints
inputs: Actual alteration backlog and worker or manager-provided availability
outputs: Verified jobs, deadlines, availability and skill constraints

steps.what: Assemble explicit job and availability fields and flag stated deadline, overlap or required-skill conflicts without assigning work automatically
inputs: S1 verified job and availability records with explicit constraints
outputs: Actual scheduling comparison and explicit conflict list

steps.what: Discuss actual alteration needs and constraints with workers and choose proposed job timing and coverage, resolving practical conflicts and exceptions
inputs: Actual scheduling comparison and real worker discussion
outputs: Actual proposed timing and coverage choices

steps.what: Write the final proposed alteration schedule using the native job and worker fields, checking dates, coverage and agreed exceptions
inputs: Actual s3 timing and coverage choices and verified job identifiers
outputs: Exact final proposed alteration schedule

steps.what: Save the final proposed schedule in the same project system without publishing assignments
inputs: Completed final proposed schedule
outputs: Stored final review version

steps.what: Review the actual completed proposed alteration schedule and decide whether to authorise its exact worker assignments and dates
inputs: S5 exact final schedule and actual scheduling authority
outputs: Actual approval or rejection of the exact schedule

steps.what: Publish only the exact authorised final alteration schedule to the internal worker assignment board
inputs: Exact final schedule and valid s6 actual scheduling authority
outputs: Actual published internal assignments and publication result

steps.what: Brief the actual alteration workers orally on the published schedule and clarify remaining practical questions
inputs: Actual published schedule and worker questions
outputs: Actual worker understanding and unresolved issues

tasks.design: Use {PROJECT} and {CALENDAR} to compare actual alteration jobs and verified availability with explicit conflict rules. The attendant makes practical choices with workers, writes the final schedule and publishes it only after the real wardrobe manager authorises that exact version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual job and availability comparisons can be assembled manually before practical choices are made.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit deadline and overlap rules and native schedule fields can reduce comparison and entry effort.
tasks.still_hard: Skills, workload and real practical conflicts require actual worker discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Make a workable schedule and explain decisions to the crew.

ambition.what: Reduce demonstrated scheduling clerical work within existing participation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: project and calendar tools can compare explicit availability and deadline fields while actual worker assignment decisions remain human work.

assumptions: Representative actual scheduling episode; no hiring decision, employment contract, training course redesign or payroll commitment is extrapolated from it. Workers and actual job owners produce availability and job requirements; s1 counts collecting, checking and mapping job ID, due date, required skill, worker ID and actual available intervals. No free clean roster is assumed.

S2 flags explicit conflicts only; it does not rank workers or allocate by inferred performance. Missing availability or skill data remains manual. Try native project/calendar rules and fields first; existing use earns no new runtime saving. Actual employee consultation and access decisions are included in rollout ranges.

S4 is actual author writing and checking, s5 ordinary ungated save. S6 must be the actual existing scheduling authority, not the author approving herself or an invented new manager. If actual scheduling rights differ, map that real route before publishing. Final version exists first; any worker, job, date or coverage change voids a1.

S7 is a distinct operative assignment publication, with its small time fully retained; s8 is actual oral briefing, not a hidden message send. Further written messages need their own actual final-version authority and send. Save share1 is negligible, fully retained and without saving.
Baseline has95 focal and5 other-role points; normalise focal savings to95. Shares are illustrative task work independent of prompt priors; schedule preparation occurs at its actual frequency.
unknowns: How much actual conflict comparison is manual today?
Who holds the real final scheduling authority?
Are availability fields current and in a comparable format?
research_questions: Observe one actual alteration schedule and count source gathering, explicit comparison, practical choices, final writing and manager authority separately.

already_counted.description: Actual source gathering, practical schedule choices, retained final writing, ordinary save, publication and worker briefing total71.2 focal points out of95.
Actual manager scheduling-authority review retains5 points, equivalent to5/95 of focal baseline.

incremental.description: Maintain availability-field mappings and explicit conflict rules beyond retained per-schedule checks.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final schedule stored in s5 including worker, job, date, time and coverage; any change requires renewed s6 authority

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:(20 comparison+19*.20 writing fields)/95*100-3=22.052, rounded down22. Low: availability arrives in inconsistent time intervals, leaving16 of20 comparison points manual and only4 comparable points automatable;4+3.8=7.8 points save,7.8/95*100-3=5.210, rounded down5.2. Actual source20, practical choices25, manager5, save1, publish1 and oral briefing9 remain. An availability-format case, unmeasured.

tasks.short: Recommend and track costume, storage or makeup budget line items

steps.what: Collect actual costume, storage and makeup needs, supplier prices and existing commitments and costs, verify coding, quantities, periods and units and specify the line-item comparison
inputs: Actual department needs, supplier quotes and existing cost and commitment records
outputs: Verified budget-line inputs and explicit calculation mapping

steps.what: Calculate explicitly mapped costume-related line totals, existing commitments, actual spend and stated differences against the current budget
inputs: S1 verified line inputs, periods and explicit quantity-price and variance rules
outputs: Source-linked line-item totals and budget comparison with missing-cost exceptions

steps.what: Assess actual costume, storage and makeup priorities and line-item pressures and choose the recommendations to give managers
inputs: Actual needs, checked budget comparison and unresolved costs
outputs: Actual budget recommendation and line-item explanation

steps.what: Write the actual working budget recommendation and line-item tracking note using native checked reference and amount fields, retaining explanation and caveats
inputs: Actual chosen recommendations and verified budget references
outputs: Actual written recommendation and line-item tracking note

steps.what: Save the working recommendation in the same document system
inputs: Completed actual working recommendation
outputs: Stored working recommendation

steps.what: Provide the actual budget recommendations to managers through the existing internal discussion and answer questions about line items and uncertainty
inputs: Actual written recommendation and manager questions
outputs: Actual manager understanding and follow-up questions

tasks.design: Use {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT} source values to calculate explicit line-item totals and variances, using {SPREADSHEET} only where it is the actual current budgeting tool. The attendant chooses recommendations, writes the actual {DOCS} note with checked fields and discusses it with managers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual cost and commitment values can require repeated table arithmetic and reference entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit budget-line arithmetic and linked document fields can perform that work deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Production needs and budget trade-offs require actual department judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Explain the consequences of underfunding a real costume or storage need.

ambition.what: Reduce demonstrated repeated line-item tracking and recommendation fields.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: explicit quantity-price totals and budget variances are deterministic; costume-budget priorities and recommendations remain human judgement.

assumptions: Representative actual recommendation and line-item review episode, not an invented full departmental reporting process. Actual suppliers provide quotes, finance records existing costs and the attendant captures real needs; s1 counts retrieval, coding, quantity/period checking and mapping. Missing quotes or commitments require real follow-up rather than a free clean feed.

S2 requires actual item/category ID, quantity, unit, price, period, currency and explicit current budget/commitment references; different tax or currency bases remain exceptions unless actual conversion rules are supplied and counted. Try native finance reports first. Existing totals or variances already generated have no new runtime saving.

Actual recommendation writing is split from managerial discussion. S6 is spoken internal presentation, not an unmodelled document send. Formal budget adoption, reallocation, purchase, payment or written distribution requires its real final-version authority and own gated action; none is hidden in tracking or saving.

The ordinary same-system save share1 is negligible, fully retained and ungated, with no author self-approval or saving. Shares are illustrative task effort independent of prompt time priors; actual overlapping finance or purchase tasks must be deduplicated when rolling up.
unknowns: Which actual line calculations are performed manually today?
Which written budget recommendation and line note actually exists?
research_questions: Observe actual line-item review and distinguish source capture, arithmetic, budget judgement, written recommendation and spoken manager discussion.

already_counted.description: Actual source capture, budget judgement, retained written recommendation, ordinary save and actual manager discussion remain in s1 and s3-s6.

incremental.description: Maintain line-item mappings and calculation checks beyond retained source and recommendation review.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:25 actual arithmetic points+14*.20=2.8 field points=27.8 gross less3 upkeep=24.8. Low: the existing finance report already covers20 of25 calculation points, leaving only5 additional manual comparison points to remove;5+2.8-3=4.8. All25 source checking,25 budget judgement,10 manager discussion and1 save remain. An existing-report coverage case specific to costume line tracking, unmeasured.

tasks.short: Assign lockers and maintain wardrobe and dressing areas

steps.what: Inspect the actual locker, dressing, wig, costume-storage or laundry area and identify usable capacity, access and physical maintenance needs
inputs: Actual rooms, lockers and physical conditions
outputs: Actual usable-space and maintenance observations

steps.what: Read actual locker occupancy, employee needs and room or locker identifiers through the existing occupancy view
inputs: Actual occupancy register and real employee requirements
outputs: Verified current locker and employee context

steps.what: Choose the actual appropriate available locker within existing assignment authority, considering real access and space requirements
inputs: Actual usable capacity, verified occupancy and employee needs
outputs: Actual locker choice

steps.what: Assign the chosen locker directly to the actual employee through the existing spoken handover and clarify access and use
inputs: Actual chosen locker and employee
outputs: Actual spoken locker assignment and handover

steps.what: Write the actual existing occupancy entry for the assignment already made, using verified employee and locker fields
inputs: Actual completed locker assignment and verified identifiers
outputs: Accurate actual occupancy entry

steps.what: Save the occupancy entry in the same room and locker register
inputs: Completed actual occupancy entry
outputs: Stored occupancy entry

steps.what: Perform the actual routine tidying, organisation and care of the dressing, wig, costume-storage or laundry area within existing duties
inputs: Actual physical area and observed routine maintenance needs
outputs: Actually maintained wardrobe area

tasks.design: Use {OPS_SYSTEM}, the existing room and locker register, to find occupancy and reuse checked locker and employee fields in the actual assignment record. Actual space inspection, locker choice, employee handover and physical area maintenance stay with the attendant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual occupancy lookup and repeated locker identifiers may require manual navigation and entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native occupancy views and form fields can reduce that clerical effort.
tasks.still_hard: Real room condition, access needs and physical maintenance require observation and work.
tasks.human_edge: Assign a usable space and notice a physical problem requiring escalation.

ambition.what: Support the existing locker assignment and routine room-care episode.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: room registers can filter actual occupancy and reuse checked identifiers while physical inspection and maintenance remain human work.

assumptions: Representative actual locker assignment and routine room-care episode with an existing occupancy register, not a measured mixture of every listed room duty. Actual staff provide employee needs and prior attendants maintain occupancy; s1 inspects real capacity, s2 checks current identities and requirements. No free clean room-status feed is assumed.

S4 is an actual spoken assignment within existing authority; s5 records it afterward. Ordinary occupancy recording does not itself grant electronic access, issue credentials or release an operative facilities order. Such real actions require their actual independent final-version authorities and separate gated steps if present.

S7 is actual routine room care, not specialist electrical repair, industrial laundry operation or hazardous work hidden inside tidying. No extra maintenance completion report is invented; if actually required, add its real post-work entry separately. The occupancy entry does not claim later maintenance completed.

Try native occupancy views and templates first. Existing features already used have zero new benefit. Same-system save share1 is negligible, fully retained, ungated and without author self-approval or saving. Shares are illustrative task work independent of prompt priors.
unknowns: Does an actual occupancy register exist and which fields are still manual?
Does any actual assignment grant electronic access requiring another authority?
research_questions: Observe actual inspection, register lookup, spoken handover, occupancy entry and routine physical room care separately.

already_counted.description: Actual inspection, retained occupancy checking, locker choice, employee handover, actual entry and save plus physical room care remain in s1-s7.

incremental.description: Maintain room and locker-view links beyond retained actual occupancy checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:15*.20+9*.10=3.9 gross less1 upkeep=2.9. Low: actual locker identifiers are informal and not mapped to the occupancy view, leaving all15 lookup and9 entry points manual; do not introduce an unhelpful view or its upkeep. All20 physical inspection,10 choice,10 handover,35 maintenance and1 save points remain. A locker-identifier mapping case, unmeasured.
